title: Inverse Modeling for Laser Pulse Shape Design in Inertial Confinement Fusion
claim: Learn a surrogate once from simulations, then train an inverse model through it so generation needs no simulator calls.
layout: 3 stacked horizontal stages, left-to-right flow, feedback loop with dashed red arrow
description: A three-band horizontal workflow figure. Band 1, "Offline preparation", runs left to right: forward simulator (cube icon) to simulation data (document stack) to "Train surrogate" (neural-net icon). Band 2, "Train the inverse model", is the largest. Desired outcomes and system properties feed a green "Inverse model" box. It proposes a candidate design, which goes into a blue "Surrogate" box marked with a lock to show it is frozen. The surrogate output goes to a "Match outcomes" circle and then to a salmon "Training feedback" box. A "Respect constraints" branch and a "Learn from examples" branch merge into that feedback. A dashed red line returns to the inverse model, labeled as the update path. Band 3, "Generate new designs", runs from a design request to a green "Trained model" to a stack of candidate designs. Green, blue and red color-code the roles. A legend distinguishes data arrows (solid) from updates (dashed).
caption: Inverse design workflow. (1) Fit an outcome surrogate to simulations. (2) Train the inverse model using examples, outcome agreement, and constraints; freeze the surrogate. (3) Generate designs from desired outcomes and system properties without simulator or surrogate calls.
abstract: The achievement of practical fusion energy remains one of the most pressing unsolved scientific challenges, with immense implications for carbon-free power. A critical factor in the success of Inertial Confinement Fusion (ICF) is the design of a Laser Pulse Shape (LP) that can optimally drive implosions under stringent physical constraints. Traditional LP design relies on computationally expensive simulations and manual iterative refinement. We introduce the ICF Laser Pulse Shape Design System (LPDS), a generative inverse modeling framework that maps desired outcomes and target pellet configurations directly to optimized LPs. Crucially, we design a multi-objective loss function to ensure the generated LPs satisfy fundamental physical constraints and experimental requirements. Furthermore, we present constraint-conditioning, inpainting, and gradient-based LP editing mechanisms for fine-grained control over specific pulse characteristics during generation. Moreover, we study the transfer of our framework to a limited set of real experimental shots. Our method establishes a data-driven inverse design framework for LP design in ICF, contributing to the advancement of practical and sustainable fusion energy.
